summary: This bill requires the VA to expand its current informed consent directive for long-term opioid therapy to also cover antipsychotics, stimulants, antidepressants, anxiolytics, and narcotics.

scores.thoughts: The bill directs a policy update within the existing Veterans Health Administration regarding informed consent procedures. It contains no provisions that authorize, expand, or reduce any government expenditures or appropriations.
The bill addresses only an internal VA clinical directive on medication consent and has no provisions related to tax policy, rates, or revenue.

The bill modifies informed-consent requirements for certain medications within the VA healthcare system. While it affects clinical practice in a public healthcare program, it does not alter coverage eligibility, funding levels, or the public-versus-private structure of care, so it does not engage the defined spectrum.
No provisions address firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
No provisions relate to immigration, visas, border policy, or immigrant protections.
No provisions address reproductive health services or abortion access.
The bill concerns VA medical policy for veterans and does not alter military or defense spending levels.
No environmental, regulatory, or climate-related provisions are present.
The bill adjusts a procedural requirement inside an existing veterans' benefit program but neither expands nor contracts eligibility or benefit levels for welfare programs.
No education policy, school funding, or school-choice provisions appear in the bill.

The bill extends informed-consent rules to narcotics and certain psychotropic medications within VA prescribing practices. This is a narrow clinical documentation requirement rather than a change in criminal penalties, decriminalization, or enforcement priorities.
No provisions address sentencing, policing, incarceration, or criminal justice reform.
No trade, tariff, or globalization measures are included.
The bill does not authorize new spending or contain any debt-reduction mechanisms.
No provisions address legal protections or rights for LGBTQ+ individuals.
No foreign-aid or international assistance provisions are present.
No voting access, election integrity, or electoral reform measures are included.
No technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight provisions appear.
No labor, union, or workplace rights provisions are present.
No provisions address religious exemptions or anti-discrimination rules.
